title: Brent Crude Tops $100/Barrel for First Time Since July as US-Iran Tanker Strikes Escalate
detail: Brent crude futures rose 2.57% to $100.44/bbl on Wednesday — the first time above $100 since July — after CENTCOM's destruction of five Iranian tankers and Iran's retaliatory missile barrage on Jordan's Al-Azraq Air Base stoked fresh fears of a broader Strait of Hormuz supply disruption. TradingEconomics recorded the price as high as ~$100.76-102/bbl intraday. Goldman Sachs said intensifying shipping attacks were raising the probability of Brent exceeding $120/bbl. The jump extends a week-long climb driven by the tit-for-tat US-Iran strikes and continued Houthi attacks on Saudi energy infrastructure.

title: IAEA Board Refers Iran to UN Security Council for First Time in 20 Years
detail: The IAEA's 35-nation Board of Governors passed a resolution reporting Iran to the UN Security Council for breaching its non-proliferation obligations — the first such referral in two decades — with 23 of 35 members in support. The resolution directs IAEA chief Rafael Grossi to transmit the resolution, prior board decisions, and his latest report to the Security Council and General Assembly, and calls on Iran to provide information and inspector access to sites bombed by Israel and the US since the war began. Iran's Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi condemned the move as based on 'fabrications,' writing on X that Western states 'attack Iran's nuclear facilities under safeguards, disrupt the normal verification process, and then use that very disruption as a pretext to issue a resolution.' Practical UN Security Council punitive measures remain unlikely since Iran's allies Russia and China hold veto power.
